newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: South Africa's Stals sees c/a deficit shrinking.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Stals sees c/a deficit shrinking.

text.p: The governor of the South African Reserve Bank Chris Stals said he believed the country's current account deficit will begin to shrink in line with a slowdown in domestic economic activity.
But he said that if there were no signs in the future that the situation was improving, the central bank would have to rethink its approach.
"If we don't see signs that the situation is improving soon, we will have to adjust our policies," he told reporters following a presentation to Swiss investors.

At the start of the month Stals said in an interview with Reuters that with a current account deficit at its current level and capital inflow at its relatively low level, the central bank could go on managing the foreign reserves for another six months or so.
However, he said then that central bank might go to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for help in covering its current account deficit.
